name: Case study — results
brief: One slide telling one client story to a prospective client: who the client is, what was wrong, what Radiant built, and what changed, in numbers. Plain, specific, confident; no superlatives the source does not earn.
placeholderArt: The three phone screenshots are the source slide's own — Newfold Digital's Account Manager app, from slide 19 — not this client's product. They stand in until this template has an image slot. Replace them by hand before this slide goes to a client.

title.label: Headline
title.brief: Start with "Case Study | ", then what was done and for whom, e.g. "Case Study | Dispatch Modernization for Acme Freight". Name the client exactly as the source does.

solutionName.label: Solution name
solutionName.brief: The name of what Radiant delivered, as a short title in the source's own terms — a product or programme name if the source gives one, otherwise a plain description.

client.label: Our Client
client.brief: One sentence: who the client is, what they do and at what scale. Facts from the source only.

problem.label: The Problem
problem.brief: Two short paragraphs. First: the situation and why it hurt the client. Second: what Radiant did about it and what that made possible. Each paragraph is shown as a bullet.

solutions.label: Solutions provided
solutions.brief: The distinct things Radiant built or introduced, one per row, most important first.

name.label: name
name.brief: A two-to-five word name for one thing delivered, e.g. "Route optimisation service".

metrics.label: Results
metrics.brief: The measured outcomes, strongest first. Only results the source states as numbers.
metrics.refusal: The row of result boxes sits under the screenshots and holds four at most.

text.label: result
text.brief: The figure in , then what it measured, e.g. "30% reduction in operational cost". Use the source's number exactly, with its qualifier ("up to", "anticipated") if it has one.
